fig3_gap_vs_cf.error_bands: shaded band = +/- 1 SD over the 5 stored seeds; available ONLY for gap_contextual and gap_matched (no seedwise arrays exist for kl_nc_floor / kl_quantum, so those two are drawn as bare lines)
fig3_gap_vs_cf.axis_decision: x axis is CF alone. 7 rows have CF=0 (lambda <= 0.50) and therefore overplot at x=0; the parameter-matched series spreads vertically there from 0 to 0.0654, which is the visual evidence that the matched gap is already positive at CF=0. A secondary lambda axis was NOT added because the CF=0 region is not representable on a CF axis.

exclusion_reasons: V=1.00 confined to panel (b) per instruction
fig6_estimators.errorbar_transformation: s3b stores `ci` as the 2.5/97.5 percentiles of the CF estimate. Plotted as (ci - cf_true) so the interval lives on the bias axis. Marker is filled when ci_contains_true is false, open when true.

exclusion_reasons: V=1.000: exceeds V_max AND status optimal_inaccurate/optimal_inaccurate
fig7_certification_loss.row_count_discrepancy: the instruction predicted 5 rows, but its own exclusion rule (drop any row whose status contains optimal_inaccurate) removes V=0.750 as well, leaving 4. The instruction's relative-gap list 4.61/7.78/9.31/7.63/2.94 likewise includes 4.61% = V=0.750. The stricter rule was applied, so 4.61% is NOT plotted. NOTE: B-1's recheck_multisolver block independently reproduced V=0.750 h_full=0.049540 with CLARABEL at clean `optimal` status, but that value is not stored as a row for this cell, so it was not used (no new computation allowed).

maximum_bracket.correction: the discrete maximum sits AT CF=0.301076 (V=0.920). For a unimodal curve the continuous maximum is bracketed by that point's NEIGHBOURS, i.e. [0.210567, 0.357645]. The instruction's narrower [0.301, 0.358] would only hold if dH(0.920) < dH(0.960), which is false (0.027741 > 0.015236). No peak marker or peak label was drawn.

fig7_certification_loss.v1000_filter_check: assertion in the script fails the build if any V=1.000 row survives; it passed.

hold_reasons: s7.json stores only n_star=980 twice (true_template and fitted_template) with NO KL attached and NO third path.
s6.json e3_collapse stores 5 rows (V = 0.75/0.80/0.856/0.92/1.00), each with M, kappa, n_star, nM_star. These are five VISIBILITY POINTS, not three 'paths'.

The three products quoted in the instruction (9.06 / 9.87 / 10.31) do not form a stored triple: 9.06 and 9.87 are s6 nM_star at V=0.856 and V=0.80, while 10.31 is not in s6 or s7 at all — it is the constant A from s7_phase1.json phase1D (a different quantity, N* ~ A/KL).
The N* = 9.30/KL baseline is not stored anywhere and 9.30 is not derivable from the stored values (s6 nM_star values are 8.987, 9.867, 9.060, 11.119, 11.547).
s6.json's own e3_summary sets formula = '붕괴 미확립 — N*(V) 테이블로만 보고', i.e. gate_s6 concluded the collapse is NOT established. Drawing a 1/KL baseline would contradict the source.
The KL_max vs CF slope-1.87 inset needs results2/gate_s7/s7_phase2c.json, which is not among the declared sources for this figure.

stored_values_available_if_reframed.note: kappa is NOT constant: 1.750 -> 0.763 across the sweep. A defensible replacement figure is N* vs M (log-log, 5 stored points) with nM_star labelled and kappa's drift shown, but that is a different claim from the instructed one, so it was not drawn without approval.

fig8_budget.recommendation: 표로 대체 권고 (as the instruction itself specifies for the missing-value branch)

exclusion_reasons: 4 quadratic directions collapsed into a single grey range band for contrast
fig4b_linear_regime.band_construction: the 4 quadratic directions have different CF grids, so each is interpolated in log-log onto a common grid over their overlap CF in [0.0050, 0.0950]; the band is the pointwise min/max.
curves_drawn_not_from_data: slope-1 reference anchored at median NC/CF = 0.1907
CF^2/6 (gate_e CHSH uniform-direction boundary limit c=1/6)
fig5a_anchors.prediction_curve_correction: the instruction named CF^2/6 as THE prediction curve, but r2.json's rel_dev (3.68% / 5.28%) is measured against the NUMERICAL reference_sweep, whose local coefficient NC/CF^2 drifts from 0.171 to 0.288 and equals 0.185 (KCBS) / 0.180 (Delft) at the anchor positions. Both curves are therefore drawn, with the numerical sweep solid (the one rel_dev refers to) and CF^2/6 thin grey dashed. Reading the quoted 3.7% / 5.3% off the CF^2/6 curve would be wrong (that comparison gives 7.0% / 13.8%).
fig5a_anchors.ci_note: the instruction quoted the KCBS CI upper end as 0.278; the stored value is 0.27954 (rounds to 0.280). The stored value is used.
fig5a_anchors.split_note: fig5_anchors 를 둘로 쪼갠 것 중 첫 번째. 앵커 2점만 남기고 N-BaIoT 18점과 인셋을 제거했다.
